method: Decode the VIN itself (any online decoder)
finding: 'The VIN identifies the vehicle, but it does not include the paint code.' Colour is stored in the maker's build record, not in the VIN characters. Generic BYD decoders (vindecoder.eu, vincario, 7zap) report no colour code in the snippets seen.
limitations: Generic, not BYD-specific; decoders not tested with a BYD VIN.
role_in_recommended_method: VIN is the KEY to a lookup (dealer/OEM system); never a source of the code itself

method: Chinese vehicle certificate (机动车整车出厂合格证) body-colour field
output_obtained: colour CLASS: one of 白/灰/黄/粉/红/紫/绿/蓝/棕/黑 (multi-colour: up to 3 colours in order)
finding: Certificate records the body colour only as a Chinese colour-class word; it cannot distinguish WA2 from W36C or a pearl white from a solid white.
limitations: Standard text read from a commercial preview; BYD's actual certificates not inspected.
role_in_recommended_method: Step 1: narrows the candidate list to the right colour family; cross-check against the catalogue colour name

method: BYD Chinese-market owner's manual: vehicle nameplate (整车铭牌) and label inventory
output_obtained: nameplate position and content list; VIN/warning/tyre-pressure label inventory
evidence_basis: 4 Chinese-market manuals read (Seal 2025, Song PLUS EV, Han L EV, Han DM-i) + 7 export manuals (Batch 5)
finding: Five manuals list the nameplate's contents (ATTO 3 2022 + the four Chinese-market manuals): company, brand, country, model, seats, build date, motor/battery data, VIN, mass (+ engine data on DM-i) - no paint/colour item. The other six export manuals only state the nameplate's position. The Seal 2025 manual's VIN-label and warning-label inventories include no colour-code label (other manuals' inventories were not read in full). Absence from a manual is not proof that no colour label exists anywhere.
limitations: Only BYD-brand models; Denza/Yangwang/Fangchengbao/Linghui manuals not found. Images not OCR'd.
role_in_recommended_method: Tells where NOT to expect the code; do not rely on the nameplate for a paint code

evidence_basis: Preview shows scope and TOC only
finding: Clause 5 'marking content' (specified + optional items) is not visible; whether colour may appear on a plate is unknown.
role_in_recommended_method: Optional: buy/read clause 5 to close the question for plates

method: Locate a printed paint/colour-code label on the vehicle
output_obtained: a code, if a label exists
evidence_basis: Retailer guidance conflicts (under bonnet / driver door-B-pillar / door jamb / service booklet); BYD manuals list none; one weak Q&A (S34) says a bonnet plate with 'paintcolor'/'H/S'
finding: No BYD source documents a paint-code label. A photographed label with the VIN plate in the same frame is the only way to turn this into VERIFIED_LABEL evidence.
limitations: Needs physical inspection of several BYD models.
role_in_recommended_method: Step 2 (parallel): inspect and photograph; record location in vin_evidence_template.csv

method: Ask a BYD service centre to read the factory colour code from the vehicle's build record by VIN
input_needed: VIN (+ ID/ownership as the shop requires)
output_obtained: expected: factory colour (name/code) from the dealer system - NOT documented by BYD
access: dealer / service centre (in person or phone)
evidence_basis: BYD's service page: 精诚钣喷 uses 原厂数据、原厂配方 with AkzoNobel/BASF/Donglai; generic dealer-VIN advice (DipYourCar); no BYD document describing the lookup
finding: The only OEM-sourced route. BYD's own repair network states it works from factory data/formulas, which implies the service system holds colour/formula data per vehicle, but no public document says that a code is shown or how staff retrieve it.
limitations: Outcome depends on what the dealer system displays (code vs formula number vs name); staff may refuse to disclose.
role_in_recommended_method: Step 3: PRIMARY route to VERIFIED_OEM evidence - capture a screenshot/photo of the system showing VIN + code + colour name; see protocol in the report

output_obtained: UNKNOWN (store listing mentions vehicle information only)
evidence_basis: App Store listing snippet; BYD page mentions app booking for 8-hour 钣喷 quick repair
finding: Not shown to expose colour or code. Test with a real account before relying on it.

method: 17vin VIN decode / EPC-level data / BYD repair-manual index
output_obtained: vehicle configuration, parts, manuals; colour output UNKNOWN
evidence_basis: About page and repair-manual index read; no decode run
finding: Plausible source of build-level data and BYD repair manuals (index lists e.g. 2017 Qin Hybrid). Never tested for colour; do not use another person's VIN.
role_in_recommended_method: Optional: test with a VIN the user owns; check the returned field list

method: AkzoNobel colour retrieval (make + year + colour code/group -> formula)
input_needed: make, year, OEM colour code or colour group
finding: The tool needs the OEM code or a colour group; it returns the formula. Formula identifiers belong to this output side.
role_in_recommended_method: Step 4: after the OEM code is known, translate to a formula

method: BASF Baslac (百事利) chips + Formula Finder; Glasurit colour chips/online
input_needed: OEM code (chips are sorted by OEM, code on the back); or visual chip match
yields_factory_paint_code: NO (formula side); chips carry the OEM code on the back
evidence_basis: Baslac chip page; Glasurit competence page
finding: Each chip = one standard formula; variants (偏差色) are darker/finer/coarser than standard - so a formula variant ID is not the OEM code. A physical chip match could reveal the code printed on the chip back without a VIN.
limitations: BYD coverage of the chip sets UNTESTED; Formula Finder not accessed (terms acceptance).
role_in_recommended_method: Step 4 and a fallback: chip match gives a candidate code with a paint-maker's own data

method: Axalta colour retrieval + Acquire spectrophotometer + fan decks
input_needed: measurement of the car, or code
output_obtained: formula (code and name printed on chip backs)
finding: A spectrophotometer reading finds a formula for the paint actually on the car - works for resprayed or faded cars but returns no factory code.
limitations: Measures current paint, not necessarily factory paint.
role_in_recommended_method: Step 5 fallback: when no code can be obtained

evidence_basis: Company background pages only; official site connection reset
finding: Donglai = Onwings (Shanghai, 688129); no public colour-lookup page found.
role_in_recommended_method: Ask a Donglai distributor which BYD colour codes/variants their system carries

method: Retailer colour finders by year/make/model (Chipex, CROP, DipYourCar, Carross, etc.)
finding: OEMatch and DipYourCar share one upstream (95% identical romanised names across shared codes); other retailers' lineage unknown. Repetition is not corroboration.
limitations: No OEM source cited by any retailer.
role_in_recommended_method: Step 0/5: source of candidate codes to test (lookup + sample plan), never of verification

output_obtained: colour names and fitment in titles
finding: Chinese retail sells pens by colour NAME and model; no code seen.
Manual says not to respray without clear damage 'to prevent mismatched colour or poor adhesion' - confirms mismatch risk but gives no code or formula.

method: Dealer confirmation protocol (PROPOSED, not a BYD procedure)
input_needed: VIN, model, MY, market, colour name from invoice, body-colour class from 合格证
yields_factory_paint_code: DEPENDS on what the dealer system shows
finding: Ask: (1) what colour name/code does the build record show for this VIN? (2) is a paint-system formula number shown, and for which maker (AkzoNobel/BASF/Donglai)? (3) can the screen or printout be photographed with the VIN visible? (4) is there any respray/repair record?
limitations: Not validated with a BYD dealer.
